featureFAQ.answer: For fullscreen, open a channel in the SavageTech TV player and press the ⛶ Fullscreen control. The player requests browser fullscreen for the video/player area. If browser fullscreen is blocked, use the browser permission/settings and try again. Landscape and Portrait are available from the player settings menu.

SavageTech TV player includes a Video Quality section in the ⚙ settings menu. Available quality choices depend on the HLS stream: the player can show Auto and any quality levels the stream actually provides. SavageTech TV cannot create a 1080p stream when the provider does not supply one.

SavageTech TV can support online subtitles when subtitle/caption tracks are available from the current stream and the browser/player supports them. Subtitles are not guaranteed for every channel because they come from the stream/provider.
The player has Landscape and Portrait screen-mode controls in the ⚙ settings menu. The exact behavior depends on browser/device orientation permissions and fullscreen support.

Open a channel card to enter the SavageTech TV player. Use Play/Pause to control playback, the sound control for audio, ⚙ for speed and quality, and ⛶ for fullscreen. HLS playback depends on browser and stream compatibility.

SavageTech TV uses HLS live streams, normally with .m3u8 playlist URLs. A channel can only play when its stream URL is reachable and compatible with the browser/player. The current player is designed for live streaming rather than on-demand movie files.

The SavageTech TV home page has a Browse Channels area with channel cards and category filtering. The current local AI directory contains the channel catalogue and can search channel names, categories and descriptions.
Use the channel search/filter area on Home to find a channel. You can also ask SavageTech AI for a channel name or category and it will search the current local channel directory.
SavageTech TV categories are Sports, Entertainment, Documentary, Religious, Kids, Movies, News and Music. Category availability and channel listings can change as the directory is updated.

SavageTech TV has Sign In and Create Account pages. A signed-in profile can keep a username, email and profile picture, and the site uses local browser storage for some preferences and recent AI chat data. If you have a password problem, use the account/recovery options available on the current login flow.

The Profile/Settings areas let a signed-in user manage profile information such as username, email and profile picture. SavageTech AI uses the signed-in username when available for personalized greetings.
The Settings page contains profile controls and preferences including Dark mode and Autoplay, plus an option to clear saved AI recent chats.

SavageTech AI is the assistant built into SavageTech TV. This build runs in local knowledge mode without requiring an OpenAI API key. It can answer SavageTech TV questions using the site knowledge and current channel directory, remember selected details on the device, and provide device/browser voice features when supported.

SavageTech AI includes a device voice mode using the browser/device speech-recognition and speech-synthesis capabilities when supported. The exact recognition language and available spoken voices depend on the device and browser.

SavageTech AI stores recent chat history and selected memory locally in the browser for the signed-in user. The Settings page includes a Clear control for AI recent chats. Clearing browser/site storage can also remove local data.

SavageTech TV has a Download page with platform options. The site should only advertise a real platform build or official link when one has actually been published; the AI should not invent a download URL.
Use the SavageTech TV Support page to contact the support inbox. The support form asks for username, email and message so the team can understand the issue.

The Privacy Policy explains information handling, local storage/preferences and third-party streams. Some SavageTech TV preferences and AI data are kept in browser local storage, while external streams may have their own policies.

The Terms of Service explains acceptance of the service terms, responsible use, streaming content, changes to the service and changes to the terms. Users should use SavageTech TV responsibly and legally.
SavageTech TV and SavageTech AI identify Victor Isack as the creator. The site support page also identifies Victor Isack as the creator of SavageTech TV.
